    Primitive projections and indecomposable module summands #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.PrimitiveSummand.trivial_subprojections_of_lift {A : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} {T : Type u_3} [Ring A] [Ring D] [AddCommGroup T] [Module D T] (p : A →+* Module.End D T) (hk : ∀ a ∈ RingHom.ker p, IsNilpotent a) {e : A} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hr : IsAtom (LinearMap.range (p e))) (b : A) (hb : IsIdempotentElem b) (heb : e * b = b) (hbe : b * e = b) :
    b = 0 ∨ b = e

    Given a lift of a projection with simple image through a homomorphism with nil kernel, every subprojection of the lift is zero or the whole lift.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.PrimitiveSummand.exists_simple_projection {D : Type u_1} {T : Type u_2} [Ring D] [AddCommGroup T] [Module D T] [IsSemisimpleModule D T] (v : T) (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (q : Module.End D T), IsIdempotentElem q ∧ IsAtom (LinearMap.range q) ∧ q v ≠ 0

    In a semisimple module, a projection onto a simple submodule detects any prescribed nonzero vector.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.PrimitiveSummand.indecomposable_range {R : Type u_1} [Ring R] {N : ModuleCat R} (e : Module.End R ↑N) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hne : e ≠ 0) (hprim : ∀ (b : Module.End R ↑N), IsIdempotentElem b → e * b = b → b * e = b → b = 0 ∨ b = e) :
    CategoryTheory.Indecomposable ↧↥(LinearMap.range e)

    The image of a nonzero primitive idempotent is indecomposable.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.PrimitiveSummand.exists_retract_detecting {R : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} {T : Type u_3} [Ring R] {N : ModuleCat R} [Ring D] [AddCommGroup T] [Module D T] [IsSemisimpleModule D T] (p : Module.End R ↑N →+* Module.End D T) (hs : Function.Surjective ⇑p) (hk : ∀ a ∈ RingHom.ker p, IsNilpotent a) (x : ↑N) (v : T) (hv : v ≠ 0) (test : ∀ (e : Module.End R ↑N), e x = 0 → (p e) v = 0) :
    ∃ (G : ModuleCat R) (r : CategoryTheory.Retract G N), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable G ∧ (ModuleCat.Hom.hom r.r) x ≠ 0

    A nonzero test vector for the action modulo a nil kernel yields an indecomposable summand on which the original vector has nonzero projection.
